chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding the beard: if it is shaved and does not grow back, then the full diyah is due; and if it grows back, then one-third of the diyah is due.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: prescribed blood-money or legal compensation for injury
key_terms.اللِّحْيَةِ: the beard, as the subject of bodily injury compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyah for shaving a man's beard if it does or does not grow back?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning compensation for injury involving the beard. If the beard is removed and does not regrow, the full diyah is due, while if it regrows, one-third of the diyah is due.
